finding: The watch reads the CI status before it reads the head, so a status of the last commit can be recorded as the result of the pushed commit.
why: Input: `start` right after a push, where ci-wait reads the final status of the last commit, the forge then moves to the pushed commit, and `_forge_behind` reads the new head; the record then holds the old status with `head_sha` of the pushed commit and `current_head: true`, which is the case D-58 exists to stop.
fix: Read the head before the ci-wait call and trust a final status only when that earlier read already showed the record's commit, as `_refuse_unless_green` already reads head first and CI second.
evidence: ci_watch.py:271 `answer = call_forge("ci-wait", ...)`, then ci_watch.py:280 `if not left or time.monotonic() - started >= HEAD_GRACE or not _forge_behind(payload, change, record):`, then _end. D-58: "2 `start` runs right after a push each ended in seconds with the status and the head of the last commit". ci-wait answers `status, elapsed, id` with no commit (afkv2/ports/forge/CONTRACT.md). The interleaving is read from the code; how often it occurs live is unverified. The Ready gate is not affected: mark-ready reads head, then CI, itself.

finding: No test starts a newer watch during the new head read and pause, and in that window the older watch overwrites the newer record.
why: The token check at line 272 runs before `_forge_behind` (a forge call) and a 15 s sleep, and line 283 then writes the old record with the old token, so a `start` in that window loses its token, its child exits as superseded, and the new commit has no watch; D-53 accepted this overwrite only because 'the window is narrow', and D-58 made it most of each wait cycle without a record. The Ready gate is not affected, because it reads CI again.
fix: Call `_is_current` again after `time.sleep(HEAD_PAUSE)` and before the beat write, and add a test whose `change-view` fake or pause starts a newer watch and then asserts that the record keeps the newer token and head.
evidence: Lines 280-283: `if not left or time.monotonic() - started >= HEAD_GRACE or not _forge_behind(payload, change, record):` ... `time.sleep(HEAD_PAUSE)` / `_write_record(path, {**record, "beat_at": time.time()})`. D-53: 'a watch can pass its token check and then overwrite the record of a `start` that lands between the check and the write. The window is narrow'. The 3 takeover tests (test_change_request.py:510, 521, 530) start the newer watch in `ci-wait` or in the last head read of `_end`, and none in `_forge_behind` or the pause. Found by reading; not run, per the brief.

finding: D-58 makes `finished` with `current_head: false` a planned end state, but the skill gives it no next action and calls it always an older commit.
why: The row says 'see below', and the text below routes only on a red CI, so an agent reports or fixes a failure of a commit that is not its own; the word 'older' is also wrong when the forge shows a newer commit than the local head, for example another person's push.
fix: Give the row a route for `current_head: false` (do not act on this status; push if the commit is not pushed, then `start`, or read CI at ship) and word it as 'another commit'.
evidence: `| `finished` | `status` is `success`, `failed` or `canceled`; `current_head: false` means an older commit: the forge did not show the pushed commit within 5 minutes, or a newer commit exists here | see below |`; the only text below is "A red CI does not stop work on the branch. Report it to the developer in one line. Fix a failure in code you own." `_report` computes `current_head` as record head == local head, with no order check.

finding: D-57 accepts an unread fix because the report 'shows' it to the developer, but no path on the way to Ready shows it.
why: `mark_ready_if_green` discards the `finish` answer and returns only id, draft, marked and url; code-review step 7 tells the agent to state only why the review stopped and what `left` holds, and a fixed finding is not in `left`; so a change can go Ready on a critical or high fix that no round read, with no message, and the test added for D-57 pins that answer.
fix: Return the unread fixes in the `mark-ready` answer and tell the skill to report them, or add them to the proofs rule in the Ship section; keep the D-57 choice of no refusal.
evidence: D-57: "the review's cap is its own rule, and its report shows the unread fix to the developer". code-review/SKILL.md step 7: "Show the developer one plain sentence: why the review stopped, and what `left` holds." review_rounds._report: `left = [entry for entry in findings if entry["outcome"] != "fixed"]`. ci_watch.py: `return ok(id=change, draft=False, marked=True, url=view.get("url") or "")`. No reader of `fixed[].reviewed` outside afkv2/skills/code-review (grep for `reviewed` over afkv2/skills).

finding: A failed head read counts as `not behind`, so the watch ends at once and can claim the status of an unverified commit with `current_head: true`.
why: Input: right after a push, ci-wait gives the final status of the last commit and change-view refuses both in `_forge_behind` and in `_end`; `_end` then falls back to the record's head, which is the local head, so the answer is `finished`, the old status and `current_head: true`, and the new test does not assert this field.
fix: On a failed head read, keep waiting until HEAD_GRACE ends, and have `_end` write an empty `head_sha` or `no-verdict` when it cannot read the head, so that `current_head` reads false; assert `current_head` in the test.
evidence: ci_watch.py:252-253 `except Refusal:` / `return False`; ci_watch.py:227-231 `head = record["head_sha"]` ... `except Refusal: pass`. test_change_request.py test_a_failed_head_read_ends_the_wait_for_the_new_commit asserts only `answer["status"] == "failed" and forge.verbs().count("ci-wait") == 1`. SKILL.md: "`current_head: false` means an older commit".

finding: test_a_push_during_the_reviews_refuses_the_mark models a local commit and no push, and the gate does not refuse a real push.
why: The fake `change-view` keeps the old head, so the refusal comes from local differing from forge; after a real push both heads move together, the second `_head_view` passes because it never compares with the first view, and the mark goes on to CI and `change-ready`, so the test name claims a behaviour the code does not have.
fix: Make the fake forge head move with the commit and assert the wanted answer: compare the 2 views' `head_sha` and refuse, or rename the test to a local commit and record in D-56 that a real push passes.
evidence: Test: `def push_during_the_review(_plan, subtask): commit(repo, f"{subtask}.txt", "late\n")` with no push and no change to `forge.answers`. Production: `_head_view` line 333 `if not local or local != view.get("head_sha")`, and line 358 `view = _head_view(payload, change)` drops the first head. Skill: 'Each push during ship goes back to step 1.' Found by reading; not run.

finding: No test reaches the `not left` branch: a final status with the forge behind and the budget ended.
why: The `forge` fixture sets `HEAD_GRACE` to 0, so every short-budget test ends on the grace clause, and the 3 tests that set a grace above 0 use the default 5400 s budget; removing `not left or` passes the suite, and then `watch` with `budget: 0` waits up to 5 minutes against its stated budget.
fix: Add a test with `HEAD_GRACE` 60, `budget=0`, `ci-wait` RED and `change-view` on another head; assert one `ci-wait`, `state: finished` and `current_head: false`.
evidence: `if not left or time.monotonic() - started >= HEAD_GRACE or not _forge_behind(...)`; fixture line 87 `monkeypatch.setattr(ci_watch, "HEAD_GRACE", 0)`. Enumeration of tests with `budget=` in a `watch` call: line 469 (`budget=100`, grace 0), line 490 (`budget=0`, STILL, the running branch), lines 1101 and 1111 (live tier, skipped without AFKV2_LIVE_CHANGE, real head). Enumeration of grace above 0: lines 422, 431, 440, all with the default budget. Mutation result is by reading; not run.

finding: The crash route covers `command-failed` only, so a crash inside the review's `finish` still routes to the developer.
why: The skill now says a crash of the review command goes to `mark-again`, but envelope.serve turns an exception inside `finish` into code `internal`, which is not in REVIEW_CAN_RETRY; for example an unretried PermissionError from os.replace in review_rounds._save reads as 'cannot clear by a run'.
fix: Add `internal` to REVIEW_CAN_RETRY, or narrow the SKILL.md row to 'gave no answer or ran past its limit'.
evidence: `+REVIEW_CAN_RETRY = {"command-failed"}`; SKILL.md: "`next: mark-again`: a post failed, or the review command crashed"; afkv2/ports/tracker/envelope.py: `except Exception as error: return fail("internal", ...)`; review_rounds.py `_save`: `os.replace(temporary, path)` with no retry. Read from code; not run.

finding: The new assertion on `LOST_AFTER` compares 3 constants and leaves out the head read and pause that this delta added to one cycle.
why: The check runs no code and states the silent time of one cycle as `SLICE + READ_MARGIN`, but a cycle now also holds a `change-view` read (limit `COMMAND_LIMIT`, 300 s) and `HEAD_PAUSE`, so it does not guard the invariant it names; the numbers still pass (1800 > 1215), and the bare `+ 60` on line 463 replaces an exact check.
fix: Assert `LOST_AFTER > SLICE + READ_MARGIN + COMMAND_LIMIT + HEAD_PAUSE`, and use `READ_MARGIN` in place of the bare 60.
evidence: `assert ci_watch.LOST_AFTER > ci_watch.SLICE + ci_watch.READ_MARGIN`; replaced line `assert reads == [(ci_watch.SLICE, ci_watch.SLICE + ci_watch.READ_MARGIN)] * 2`; ci_watch.py:22-29 constants.

finding: D-57's capped review is proved only on a hand-written report, with fields the gate does not read, and never on the real review command.
why: If `review_rounds.py` starts to leave a capped fix in `left.blocking`, this test stays green and Ready is refused with no route to clear, which is the case D-57 exists to prevent; the `real_review` fixture is there and 3 real rounds can drive it.
fix: Drive the real command to `stopped_by: cap` through `real_review` (3 rounds, a high finding `fixed` in round 3) and assert `marked` and `fixed[0].reviewed` is False.
evidence: `ship["reviews"]["0001-a"] = {**SETTLED, "stopped_by": "cap", "fixed": [{"id": "f1", "sha": "abc", "reviewed": False}]}`; `_why_open` reads only `left`, the truth of `stopped_by`, and `change`. Today the shape is correct: review_rounds.py:319-320 and 334-336 give `cap`, `reviewed: false` and an empty `left.blocking` (read, not run).

finding: The child-process test no longer shows that the record takes its head from the forge, because the stub head now equals the local head.
why: The record starts with the local head, so a broken `_end` head read gives the same `head_sha`; the old value `from-the-forge` told the 2 apart, and no real child-process or real-port test does so now, only the in-process fake at line 436.
fix: Assert something only the forge read can give, for example a stub title or a record field, or drive the real port in process with a forge head that differs and a short `HEAD_GRACE`.
evidence: Removed: `assert code == 0 and answer["status"] == "failed" and answer["head_sha"] == "from-the-forge"`. Added: `answer["head_sha"] == git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")`, with stub `"headRefOid": {git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")!r}`. `Tools` in `real_port` also answers the local head (line 1046).
